Complete neutralisation first, then evaluate the remaining weak-base buffer:
\[pOH=pK_b+\log_{10}\frac{[\ce{NH4+}]}{[\ce{NH3}]}.\]
For emission from initial level \(n_i\) to final level \(n_f\), the photon wavenumber is \(\widetilde\nu=R(n_f^{-2}-n_i^{-2})\).

The higher-concentration copper(II) half-cell is reduced and the lower-concentration half-cell is oxidised. The standard electrode potentials cancel. The concentration ratio is 100 and the electron count is two, giving the displayed potential of 0.0591 V. The cell reaction reduces the concentration difference.
